The test image shows a collapsed tomato plant with:
- Severely wilted/prostrated whole plant with roots exposed
- Pale/bleached whitish stem - very prominent
- Some brown lesions on stems
- Dried, brown leaves
- Predominantly a stem/whole plant presentation

This points to stem-based diseases. Top candidates: **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**, **Southern_Blight**, **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt**, **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers**.

Now viewing one reference from each candidate:

Note the Bugwood image number in test image is **1568040**, and the Southern_Bacterial_Wilt stem reference I just saw is **1568041** — consecutive numbers from the same series. This strongly suggests the same disease. Let me check the fourth reference for confirmation.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image (Bugwood 1568040)**: Shows a tomato plant collapsed/pulled from ground, roots exposed, stems appearing pale/whitish with some brown lesions. Entire plant has wilted and died.
- **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt stem ref (Bugwood 1568041)**: Consecutive image number from the same Bugwood series — shows cross-section of stem with brown vascular discoloration, confirming the disease.
- The collapsed whole plant with exposed roots matches Southern Bacterial Wilt's end-stage (permanent wilt after vascular discoloration and root rot).
- Sclerotinia would show white cottony mycelium and black sclerotia (not visible).
- Southern Blight would show white mycelium mats and sclerotia at soil line (not visible).
